q1_issues.issue: "The same goes for X" is a fixed anaphoric construction whose literal reading (something physically going) is incoherent for these participants, so the idiom coherence test forbids unpacking it into a literal go event with a For oblique.

"the same" points at a previously stated predication, not an entity, so typing it as a sk_thing_1 witness invents a referent the sentence never introduces and drops the sentence's whole content (that the prior claim also holds of animals).

q2_gaps: anaphora to a prior predication / predicate ellipsis ("the same goes for X", "so does Y", "likewise", "ditto") — the instruction set has no way to assert that a previously stated proposition also holds of a new argument; its coreference section covers entity and event anaphora only, and its idiom rule (one fused surface symbol) does not fit a construction with its own subject and argument
notes: Mechanically the atoms are well formed — the untyped referent gets its mandatory thing class atom, For is a legitimate preposition-named oblique, and the simple present correctly takes no status atom. The failure is at the construction level, not the atom level.
